feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the horizontal asymptote of $y={5}^{x-a}+b$ is $y=b.$ 

In the figure above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=\frac{3}{2}.$ Hence, $b=\frac{3}{2}.$

Next, we use the point $(3,\frac{5}{2})$ to determine the value of $a.$
Substituting $(3,\frac{5}{2})$ into the equation of the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{3-a}+\frac{3}{2} & =\frac{5}{2} \\ {5}^{3-a} & =1 \\ 3-a & =0 \\ a & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a=3$ and $b=\frac{3}{2}.$
